_note: Week of Nov. 16 capsules, written from the frozen fact sheet in 2026-11-16.json.
new-mexico:
New Mexico is No. 1 in the Mountain West in a ranking built to reward road wins, and the Lobos do not have one. That is the first thing to understand about this team, and the second is that it does not seem to matter. Recent form puts New Mexico at plus-13.9 points a game against an average Division I team, the best in the league by a point and a half, and that is the entire index. No bonus required.

The week had a little of everything. On Tuesday the Lobos beat Little Rock 94-69 at home, a 25-point win of the sort the model believes in. On Saturday they went to Santa Clara and lost 90-85, a five-point road loss to a West Coast Conference team. They are 3-1, and the road ledger is empty.

The headline is a sophomore guard named Jake Hall, who is averaging 27.8 points a game over four games. That is not a typo. It is the highest scoring average of any player in the four leagues we rank, and it is the kind of number that makes opposing coaches spend their film sessions drawing circles around one name.

What makes the Lobos dangerous is that Hall is not alone. Hudson Mayes, another sophomore guard, adds 16.2 points and 6.5 rebounds. Uriah Tenette, a third sophomore guard, is at 15.2. Three sophomores averaging more than fifteen a night is a team built for this season and the two after it.

The week brings one game, and it is the right kind. On Saturday New Mexico plays at Wichita State, a road game against a program with a long memory and a loud building.

A win there would put the first entry on the road ledger and make the Lobos' lead even harder to argue with. They are already first without the bonus. Imagine what happens when they start collecting it.
grand-canyon:
Grand Canyon is 4-0 and second in the Mountain West, and the Lopes have done it the old-fashioned way: by winning at home, by a lot, and letting the model do the arithmetic. On Wednesday they beat Cal Poly 99-71. On Saturday they beat UL Monroe 88-52. Twenty-eight and thirty-six. Recent form is plus-12.3 points a game against an average Division I team, second in the league only to New Mexico. There are no road wins yet, so that is the entire index.

The Lopes have not been tested on the road. They have also not been tested at home, in the sense that nobody has come within twenty of them in the last week. That is not their fault. It is just what the Index cannot see yet.

The roster is built on experience. All three leading scorers are senior guards. Jaden Henley leads at 17.8 points and 3.5 rebounds. Makaih Williams adds 13.0 points in three games. Dylan Darling is at 11.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 5.2 assists, the playmaker of the group and the player who makes the other two look so comfortable.

Three senior guards in a backcourt is the sort of thing that wins in March, because seniors have seen most things a defense can do and know how to stay calm when the building gets loud. In November, it mostly means the Lopes do not beat themselves.

Our schedule shows no games for Grand Canyon this week, which means the Lopes will hold their number while everyone around them plays. A frozen form score in a league this crowded at the top is a curious thing; the teams below them get a week to catch up, and the teams above them get a week to pull away.

When the Lopes do take the floor again, the first road game will be the one to watch. The formula is patient. It is waiting for them to leave Phoenix.
wyoming:
Wyoming went to Chapel Hill on Tuesday and lost to North Carolina, 76-63, which is the sort of road trip a mid-major makes to find out exactly where it stands. Four days later the Cowboys went to Denver and won 76-53, a 23-point road win that put 0.7 points a game on the ledger. They are 3-1, and the Bricks Index has them third in the Mountain West.

Recent form is plus-8.9 points a game against an average Division I team, a figure that takes the North Carolina loss seriously, since a thirteen-point loss on that floor is a respectable night by any measure. Add the road credit and Wyoming sits at plus-9.6.

The Cowboys are young where it counts. Nasir Meyer, a sophomore guard, leads at 14.8 points, 5.5 rebounds and 3.2 assists, the all-around line of a player who fills every column of the box score. Gavin Gores, a sophomore forward, adds 10.8 points. Khaden Bennett, a senior guard, is at 10.2 points, 5.8 rebounds and 3.0 assists, the veteran who does the same thing Meyer does with a few more years of practice.

Two guards who rebound and pass is a backcourt that can hold its own against bigger teams, and the North Carolina game suggested that Wyoming will not be pushed around by anyone this season.

The week brings two games. On Tuesday Sam Houston comes to Laramie, a home game at altitude that visiting teams tend to remember for their lungs as much as the score. On Sunday the Cowboys meet Duquesne on a neutral floor, a game that counts half on the road ledger.

The Denver win was the kind the formula loves: away from home, by a lot, against a Division I team. Another one like it on Sunday, even at half credit, and the Cowboys will start looking up at the top two rather than over their shoulder.
nevada:
Nevada has lost two straight, and the Bricks Index still has the Wolf Pack fourth in the Mountain West, which says a great deal about what the Wolf Pack did before the losses. On Nov. 8 they beat Saint Mary's 96-95 on a neutral floor, a one-point win over one of the West Coast Conference's most consistent programs. Even at half credit for the neutral site, the win is worth 1.1 points a game, the most road credit in the league this week. Recent form is plus-6.8. The total is plus-7.9.

The week was less kind. On Wednesday Nevada went to UC Santa Barbara and lost 76-63. On Saturday they came home and lost to Utah Valley, 73-71, a two-point game that could have gone the other way. They are 2-2.

The backcourt leads the way. Styles Phipps, a junior guard, is averaging 19.0 points, 4.2 rebounds and 4.8 assists, the kind of line that makes a player the first name on a scouting report. Vaughn Weems, a senior guard, adds 16.0 points. Elijah Price, a junior forward, is at 11.0 points and 6.8 rebounds.

Phipps and Weems together are scoring 35 points a night, and on a team that has played close games against good opponents, that kind of scoring is what keeps you in every one of them.

The Saint Mary's game showed what Nevada is capable of. The Utah Valley game showed how thin the line is between a win and a loss in November. Both are true at once, which is what makes the first month of the season so hard to read and so much fun to watch.

The week brings one game. On Wednesday Idaho comes to Reno, a home game against a regional opponent that the Wolf Pack will very much want to win after last week.

The streak is two. Phipps will have the ball on Wednesday. Nevada would like to end the streak before it becomes a story.
unlv:
UNLV is 3-0 and fifth in the Mountain West, and the Rebels have not yet left home. The only game last week was a 76-68 win over Stanford on Friday, an eight-point win over an ACC team that the model takes seriously. Recent form is plus-3.7 points a game against an average Division I team. No road wins yet, so that is the whole index.

That is a team doing what it should at home, and the Index is waiting, with some interest, to see what happens when it travels.

The scoring is concentrated and potent. Sebastian Mack, a senior guard, leads at 21.0 points a game, one of the highest averages in the league. Cam Miles, a sophomore guard, adds 17.3 points. Tyrin Jones, a sophomore forward, is at 15.0 points and 6.3 rebounds. Three players averaging fifteen or more is an offense that can come at a defense from several directions, and that is a hard thing to stop over forty minutes.

The pairing of a senior star with two sophomores is the kind of roster that tends to get better as the season goes on. Mack knows how to win. Miles and Jones are learning, and the early numbers suggest they are learning quickly.

The week brings the biggest game on the Mountain West card. On Tuesday UNLV meets Kansas on a neutral floor. A neutral-site win counts half on the road ledger, and against a program like Kansas, even half would be a significant number.

A loss would cost the Rebels very little. A win would rearrange the top of this ranking. That is the kind of asymmetry the formula was designed to reward, and UNLV has the scorers to make it interesting.

Mack has played in big games before. The question is whether the sophomores are ready for the brightest lights they have seen this season. Tuesday will tell.
hawaii:
Hawai'i is 3-1 and sixth in the Mountain West, with a Bricks Index of exactly zero, which is the formula's way of saying the Rainbow Warriors have been precisely average against the teams they have played. The minus sign in front of the zero is a rounding error and nothing more.

The only game last week was a 73-66 home loss to Portland on Monday, a seven-point loss that the model took at full weight. There are no road wins on the ledger, so the index is all recent form.

Average is not a criticism in November. It is a starting point, and it means the Rainbow Warriors have neither surprised the model nor disappointed it. The rest of the season will decide which direction they go from here.

The scoring runs through a junior forward. Zack Davidson is averaging 17.5 points and 4.5 rebounds, the inside presence that the offense is built around. Chance Trujillo, a junior guard, adds 14.0 points and 3.2 assists. Jaden Matingou, a senior guard, is also at 14.0 in three games. Three players averaging fourteen or more is a balanced attack, and balance tends to hold up on the long road trips that are a fact of life for a team in Honolulu.

That travel is worth a word. No team in college basketball has to cross more water to play a road game, and the Index pays for road wins precisely because they are hard. For Hawai'i, every road win is earned twice.

The week brings one game. On Wednesday the Rainbow Warriors meet Washington State on a neutral floor, a game that counts half on the road ledger and would be the first entry on it.

A win there would push the number above zero for the first time. A loss would push it below. Either way, the Rainbow Warriors will have a clearer idea of who they are by the weekend. Zero is a fine place to start. It is not a place anyone wants to stay.
uc-davis:
UC Davis has won three straight, and on Saturday the Aggies made the short drive across the Yolo Causeway and beat Sacramento State 75-56, a nineteen-point road win over a neighbor that put 0.4 points a game on the ledger. Earlier in the week, on Wednesday, they beat Incarnate Word 81-69 at home. They are 3-1.

The Bricks Index has the Aggies at minus-3.0 points a game, seventh in the Mountain West. Recent form, at minus-3.4, still carries the weight of the season-opening loss, and the road credit softens it a little.

That is a team on the way up. The model's short memory means every win this week counts more than the loss two weeks ago, and if the streak keeps going, the number will keep climbing.

The scoring is spread across the lineup. Connor Sevilla, a senior guard, leads at 13.5 points a game. Jalen Stokes, a sophomore guard, adds 11.8 points and 5.2 rebounds. Veniamin Abosi, a junior forward, is at 11.0 points and 7.2 rebounds. Three players between eleven and fourteen points is the profile of a team that wins without a star, by moving the ball until somebody has a good look.

That kind of team tends to travel well, because it does not depend on one player's shooting night. The Sacramento State game, won by nineteen in a building full of people who would very much have liked the other result, was a good example.

The week brings one game. On Tuesday Alabama State comes to Davis, a home game against a Division I opponent from the SWAC.

It will not move the road ledger. It will move the form number, and for a team on a three-game streak, that is the number that matters most right now. The Aggies are climbing. Tuesday is another rung.
san-jose-state:
San José State is 2-2 and eighth in the Mountain West, and the week showed both versions of the Spartans in the same building. On Thursday UC Riverside came to San José and won 80-75, a five-point home loss the model took at full weight. On Sunday Alabama State visited and the Spartans won 80-68. There are no road wins yet, so the Bricks Index is all recent form: minus-4.0 points a game.

A split at home in November is not a verdict. It is a team still working out which five players should be on the floor at the end of a close game.

The backcourt does most of the work. Mekhi Mason, a senior guard, leads at 18.5 points a game. Joey Chammaa, a junior guard, adds 17.2 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.5 assists, the all-around line of a player who runs the offense and scores in it. Zine Eddine Bedri, a senior forward, is at 10.2 points.

Mason and Chammaa together are scoring nearly 36 points a night, which makes the Spartans one of the more dangerous guard tandems in the league. The question is what happens when a defense takes one of them away, and that is a question the next few weeks will answer.

The week brings two games, and both are interesting. On Wednesday Fresno State comes to San José, an old in-state opponent and a game with plenty of history behind it. On Sunday the Spartans meet Loyola Chicago on a neutral floor, a game that would count half on the road ledger and be the first entry on it.

A win over Fresno State would mean something to the people in the building. A win over Loyola Chicago would mean something to the formula. Both would mean something to a team that has not yet strung together two good nights in a row.

Mason and Chammaa have the scoring. The Spartans need the rest of the floor to give them a reason to believe in a streak.
utep:
UTEP is 2-1 and ninth in the Mountain West, and the Miners spent last week winning the only kind of game that matters in El Paso in November. On Thursday they beat New Mexico State 60-58 at home, a two-point win in the Battle of I-10, the rivalry that the two programs have played for longer than most of their players have been alive. It was the only game of the week.

The Bricks Index has the Miners at minus-6.0 points a game, all recent form, no road credit. That number does not care about rivalries, only margins, and a two-point win at home does not move it much.

The scoring runs through a sophomore. Cam McDaniels, a guard, is averaging 20.0 points a game over three games, one of the highest averages in the league. Youssouf Traore, a freshman forward, adds 12.7 points and 7.0 rebounds, a first-year big man already doing a starter's work on the glass. Leif Moeller, a sophomore guard, is at 8.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.7 assists.

A sophomore scorer and a freshman rebounder is a young core, and young cores tend to make the most progress between November and February. The Miners are not a finished product. They are not supposed to be.

The week brings two games and a rematch. On Monday, the day this ranking was frozen, Florida A&M visits. On Thursday UTEP goes back up Interstate 10 to Las Cruces for the second half of the rivalry, this time on New Mexico State's floor.

The Las Cruces game is the one the Index will pay for. A road win over a rival is worth exactly what any other road win is worth to the formula, and quite a bit more to everyone in El Paso.

McDaniels will have the ball. The Miners will have the memory of Thursday. The Aggies will have the home crowd. It should be a very good night.
air-force:
Air Force scored 107 points on Wednesday, and if you have spent any time watching the Falcons over the years, that sentence is worth reading twice. The 107-93 home win over Loyola Chicago was the kind of shootout that does not usually happen in Colorado Springs. Four days later Air Force went to Pacific and lost 93-69. The Falcons are 3-2, and the Bricks Index has them tenth in the Mountain West at minus-7.2 points a game, all recent form, no road credit.

That is a team whose two games last week looked like they came from two different seasons, and the model averages them into a number that does not quite describe either one.

The scoring is young and spread out. Kam Sanders, a sophomore guard, leads at 19.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 4.8 assists, the all-around line of a player who does everything the offense needs. Grant Best, a freshman guard, adds 16.0 points and 4.8 rebounds. Lucas Hobin, a sophomore forward, is at 15.8 points. Three players averaging nearly sixteen or more, and not one of them is a senior.

That is a core with time ahead of it. A sophomore who scores nearly twenty and a freshman who scores sixteen are the kind of foundation that a program can build around for three years, and the Falcons have both.

The week brings one game. On Saturday Air Force goes to UTSA, a road game in San Antonio and a chance to put the first entry on the road ledger.

A win there would move the Falcons off the bottom of this ranking and give the Index something to work with besides two very different results. A loss would leave them where they are, with a talented young roster still learning how to win away from home.

Sanders will have the ball. The question is which version of the Falcons shows up in Texas: the one that scored 107, or the one that lost by 24.
